name: Venn possible cases
statement: \text{Draw every Venn case allowed by the statements; a conclusion follows only if it holds in every case (a 'possibility' if it holds in at least one).}
derivation: Draw the minimal diagram: All A are B = A inside B; Some A are B = A and B overlap; No A is B = A and B apart.
Mark the parts that are fixed and the parts that may or may not exist.
Definite conclusion: true in every case. 'Some B are A' follows from 'All A are B' and from 'Some A are B'.
Possibility conclusion: true in at least one case and not ruled out by any statement.
A term not in the statements (postcards) can never give a definite conclusion.
visual_proof: Each statement places one circle inside, across or apart from another; a conclusion is valid when every allowed drawing shows it.

steps: All fans are brown: Fans circle inside Brown, so some brown are fans (I follows).
Some brown are chairs: the overlap exists both ways, so some chairs are brown (II follows).
Some chairs are plastic directly contradicts 'No chair is plastic' (III fails).

common_traps: Reading 'All A are B' as 'All B are A'.
Accepting 'No chair is plastic' when a statement says some chairs are plastic.
Taking a possibility ('all tears being streams') as false because it is not certain.
Concluding 'Some A are C' from 'Some A are B' and 'Some B are C' (the overlaps need not meet).

diagram.alt_text: Venn diagram of Fans, Brown and Chairs: the parts of Fans outside Brown are empty; Brown and Chairs overlap, and whether that overlap includes fans is open.

name: Either-or complementary pair
statement: \text{If two conclusions about the same two classes are each uncertain but exactly one must hold (Some/No or All/Some-not), answer 'either I or II follows'.}
conditions: Both conclusions are about the same two classes
The pair is complementary: Some/No or All/Some-not
derivation: Test I and II separately with [[f:syllogism.venn-cases]]; neither may follow by itself.
Check they share the same subject and predicate (pens and bags in both).
Check they are complementary: 'Some A are B' / 'No A is B', or 'All A are B' / 'Some A are not B'.
In every possible diagram one of them is true and the other false, so the answer is 'either I or II'.
visual_proof: With Pens inside Books and Books meeting Bags, the Pens-Bags overlap may or may not exist: one drawing makes 'Some pens are bags' true, the other makes 'No pen is a bag' true.
common_traps: Marking 'either' when one conclusion already follows; then that one alone is the answer.
Pairing 'Some A are B' with 'Some A are not B': both can be true, so they are not complementary.
Pairing conclusions about different classes ('Some pens are bags' / 'No book is a bag').
Marking 'neither follows' when the pair is complementary.

diagram.alt_text: Venn diagram of Pens, Books and Bags: Pens lies inside Books, Books overlaps Bags, and the region shared by Pens and Bags is only possible, so exactly one of 'Some pens are bags' and 'No pen is a bag' holds.

verification.code:
from itertools import product

def models(sets, statements):
    """Every Venn model: each of the 2^n regions empty or non-empty, all classes non-empty."""
    n = len(sets)
    regions = list(product([0, 1], repeat=n))[1:]           # the outside region is irrelevant
    idx = {s: i for i, s in enumerate(sets)}
    for occ in product([0, 1], repeat=len(regions)):
        live = [r for r, o in zip(regions, occ) if o]
        if all(any(r[i] for r in live) for i in range(n)) and all(st(live, idx) for st in statements):
            yield live, idx

def All(a, b):  return lambda L, I: not any(r[I[a]] and not r[I[b]] for r in L)
def Some(a, b): return lambda L, I: any(r[I[a]] and r[I[b]] for r in L)
def No(a, b):   return lambda L, I: not any(r[I[a]] and r[I[b]] for r in L)
def Not(f):     return lambda L, I: not f(L, I)

def follows(sets, statements, conclusion, possibility=False):
    ms = list(models(sets, statements))
    assert ms, "statements are inconsistent"
    hits = [conclusion(L, I) for L, I in ms]
    return any(hits) if possibility else all(hits)

def either_or(sets, st, c1, c2):
    ms = list(models(sets, st))
    a = [c1(L, I) for L, I in ms]
    b = [c2(L, I) for L, I in ms]
    if all(a) or all(b):
        return False                       # one follows by itself: not an either-or answer
    return all(x != y for x, y in zip(a, b))   # exactly one is true in every case

# Constructed: All pens are books. Some books are bags.  I. Some pens are bags.  II. No pen is a bag.
S = ["pen", "book", "bag"]
st = [All("pen", "book"), Some("book", "bag")]
assert not follows(S, st, Some("pen", "bag")) and not follows(S, st, No("pen", "bag"))
assert either_or(S, st, Some("pen", "bag"), No("pen", "bag"))
found = "either" if either_or(S, st, Some("pen", "bag"), No("pen", "bag")) else "neither"
options = {"A": "only I", "B": "only II", "C": "either", "D": "neither"}
assert [k for k, v in options.items() if v == found] == ["C"]

# Boundary: when one conclusion follows on its own, the answer is that one, not 'either'.
st2 = [All("pen", "book"), All("book", "bag")]
assert follows(S, st2, Some("pen", "bag")) and not either_or(S, st2, Some("pen", "bag"), No("pen", "bag"))
# Boundary: the pair must be about the same two classes; Some pens are bags / No book is a bag is no pair.
assert not either_or(S, st, Some("pen", "bag"), No("book", "bag"))
# Boundary: a non-complementary pair (Some / Some-not) can both be true, so no 'either'.
assert not either_or(S, st, Some("pen", "bag"), Not(All("pen", "bag")))
# All / Some-not is the other complementary pair.
assert either_or(S, st, All("pen", "bag"), Not(All("pen", "bag")))
print("BOUNDARY_OK")
